structure.structure_requirement: At least 3 nonempty finite meshes, all meshes finite and all object matrices finite
structure.group_interpretation: Structural operability only; no claim of semantic or true 3D recovery

target.rule: lexicographically first non-root EMPTY with >=2 nonstructural finite mesh descendants

approximate_relations.limitation: AABB candidates only, not true mesh contact/collision; no ground truth support labels

hierarchy_parts.meaning: Integrity of emitted part declarations; not completeness against reference image

known_support.meaning: Declared support; normalized AABB contact approximation, not true mesh support

mesh_intersection.meaning: Triangle surface crossings; intended joints may also intersect. No containment test or semantic collision truth; supplemental, not hard gate

structure.measurement_limit: AABB extents are approximate, not collision tests; unknown scale, no metric 3D accuracy

failure_evidence.attribution: Stage/log evidence only. Scene build timeout without finer events is not proven Boolean/mesh overload.
failure_evidence.quality_interpretation: Continuous measured Q is not geometry truth; infrastructure errors do not identify a visual module

visual_findings.observation: The backrest is blue in reconstruction 2 but pale green in reference 1. The legs and separate right-hand block also change from green to blue, while the seat remains blue.
visual_findings.hypothesis: A material edit may have propagated through a shared material. The supplied local_material function edits the existing material without copying it, and the backrest, seat, legs, and right-hand block all list SceneActSurface_0.

alternatives.explanation: The backrest could have received an incorrect blue material assignment directly, independently of shared-material propagation.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: The isolated backrest remains blue; isolation cannot distinguish direct assignment from a shared-material edit.

alternatives.explanation: Scene-dependent illumination or reflected blue light could contribute to the apparent color, although the supplied blue base color makes this less likely as the main cause.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: Removing other meshes reduces their reflected-light contribution; the hue could move toward the reference if that contribution drives the mismatch.

visual_findings.probe_reason: Isolating Box.001 tests whether the blue appearance persists without other mesh contributions. Persistence supports an intrinsic material explanation but cannot identify which material-edit mechanism occurred. Evaluate backrest hue, not full-image similarity after isolation.
visual_findings.mapping_evidence: Box.001 is the sole mesh under Back; its broad, thin, elevated geometry and projected bounds correspond to the visible backrest. Its listed shader base color is blue.
visual_findings.uncertainty: The visible color discrepancy is clear, but the images and material snapshot do not establish the edit history or unique cause. Isolation also changes indirect illumination and cannot recover the reference material.
